concepts.def: Area of land drained by a river and its tributaries; open subsystem of water cycle.
Time between peak rainfall and peak discharge.

Groundwater seepage maintaining river flow between storms.

walkthroughs.body_html: Annual UK precipitation averages about 1150 mm; evapotranspiration about 400 mm; the rest becomes runoff and groundwater recharge. Soil moisture deficit develops in summer when evapotranspiration exceeds rainfall.

Flashy hydrographs (short lag, high peak) occur in urbanised, impermeable basins. Subdued hydrographs (long lag, low peak) characterise vegetated, permeable basins. Urbanisation in the Don catchment, Sheffield reduced lag from hours to minutes.

The Tees rises on impermeable Carboniferous millstone grit in Cumbria. Cow Green Reservoir regulates flow. Storm Desmond (2015) brought 341 mm in 24 hours to Honister Pass, producing record peak flows and flooding Carlisle.
